steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Coat a baking sheet with cooking spray.
Wipe mushrooms with a damp paper towel; carefully remove stems. Chop stems extremely fine, discarding tough stem ends.

Heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add chopped mushroom stems and garlic; cook, stirring often, until the stems are tender and any released moisture has evaporated. Take care not to let the garlic burn. Remove from the heat and let cool slightly.
Stir cream cheese, Parmesan cheese, black pepper, onion powder, and cayenne pepper into the mushroom mixture until well combined. The filling will be very thick.
Spoon the cream cheese filling into the mushroom caps, mounding it slightly. Arrange the filled mushroom caps on the prepared baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until mushroom caps are tender and the filling is hot, about 20 minutes.
Let the mushrooms cool for a few minutes before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Mouth-Watering Stuffed Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: These easy stuffed mushrooms are filled with a savory blend of cream cheese, Parmesan, garlic, and mushroom stems for a crowd-pleasing appetizer.

video.description: Make this restaurant-quality appetizer for your next big dinner party. In this video, the Allrecipes team shows you how to make mouth-watering stuffed mushrooms with minced garlic, Parmesan cheese, and more!
video.name: How to Make Mouth-Watering Stuffed Mushrooms

review.reviewBody: I've made these many times and everyone loves them. They are not time consuming at all and can be made up two days before needed. Wash mushrooms and twist out stems. Drain in colander. Put mushroom caps on paper towels to drain well. Slice off woody part of stem and put in food processor. Pulse stems until minced. Add 1 Tlbs olive oil to pan and stir-fry minced stems and garlic (minced type from jar)until dry. Add spices. Slightly cool, but while still warm add cheeses (and a can of drained crab if want). Put a plastic zip lock bag into a bowl and roll back sides- add cream cheese mixture. Snip off one corner and use as a pastry bag to fill mushrooms. If making ahead 1)use only freshest mushrooms you can find, 2)blot off excess water from mushrooms, 3)put them into a non-metalic dish. I sprinkle the tops with shreded (not grated )parmesan cheese. Cover well with plastic wrap and refrig. until ready to bake. (I've made up to two days in advance- without crabmeat though).

This was my first time making stuffed mushrooms and after reading several of the reviews I decided on how I would make mine. The full amount of cream cheese was enough for 24 mushrooms and I placed a bit of chopped proscuitto in the bottom of each mushroom before placing the cheese mixture on top (which was wonderful). I then sprinkled garlic and herb bread crumbs over them and drizzled melted butter over all. Baked for only 15 minutes and broiled for the last 5. They were wonderful. I plan on making these when my Mom and Grandmom come to visit in the fall. Thanks a bunch!

Excellent recipe. I doubled the filling and used 24 oz fresh mushrooms and it filled them almost perfectly. I also added a dash of Worcestershire sauce while cooking the stems and 1/3 cup of crumbled bacon to the cream cheese mixture. Just before baking, I sprinkled with breadcrumbs and dipped the mushroom caps in melted butter so that they wouldn't dry out. I brought to Thanksgiving as an appetizer and they went in minutes. Everyone loved the bite that the cayenne pepper added. Thanks for the great recipe!

I have made these many times, and they always disappear so fast! What a great recipe. I put the stuffing into a ziploc bag with a corner cut off and squeeze it into the caps, it's less messy. Thanks for sharing such a great treat!

Wonderful--gone in minutes at a party. 1st off, you need 30 button mushrooms (2 pkgs)...I read almost all the reviews, and can't understand who would put all that stuffing in 12 mushrooms. They complained it was too cream-cheesy...use common sense. How did anyone even do it...the mushrooms had to be falling over from being so top-heavy. Second, I added about 10 chives (chopped), omitted the stems, topped with Italian breadcrumbs, and most importantly, tossed the mushrooms in a melted butter/1 tbs lemon juice mixture before stuffing and baking. As a few suggested, use a Ziploc and cut off a small portion of the corner to stuff...you're done in no time and no mess. They came out delicious.

I used less cream cheese (4 oz) and I added some GF flavored bread crumbs (about a half cup). Otherwise, left the recipe the same. Brush mushrooms with olive oil and position in a (small) muffin tray to help hold shape while cooking. Delicious!

I've made these stuffed mushrooms twice now. They are soooo good. The cream cheese filling is absolutely divine. I used a food processor to chop the stems (let's be real - who has time to finely chop mushroom stems by hand?) by pulsing so they didn't get too liquid-y. I also rolled the stuffed tops in Italian bread crumbs for some texture before baking but they'd be delicious without that, as well. I'll be coming back to this recipe again and again.

Made these for the Superbowl and they are delicious! I mixed melted butter & the filling seasonings along with panko and dipped the tops of the mushrooms in the panko mixture for a crunchy texture. Love!

These were soooooo good! I got 14 large mushrooms out of it. I read all the reviews first and cooked up 3 pieces of thick sliced bacon. After I took those out I cooked the garlic and stems in the bacon grease. I also added green onions, about double the onion powder and probably about double the amount of Parmesan. I sprinkled panko bread crumbs on top. I liked it so much I went and bought more cream cheese today. For the record, I am absolutely not a mushroom lover. I made them for my partner and neither of us could get enough of them! I might add more spices next time as it was still a bit cream cheesy. But it was delicious and I’m sure they’d be delicious without any changes!

I had a dinner to go to at a friend’s house and this popped up in an email. I had a couple packs of mushrooms that needed to be used so I gave it a shot. I am a bit of a mad scientist in the kitchen and I had some goat cheese leftover from Thanksgiving so I threw that in the mix. I also added a little tapenade of olive, basil and cheese. I sprinkled smoked paprika on top but then decided to add the Panko. I did a little spritz of olive oil spray and baked. They turned out great! Everyone loved them and they vanished. I think next time I will add a little parm to the panko before I dip the tops. I was worried it might get too salty with the tapenade but it wasn’t at all. Because I added the goat cheese to the cream cheese I had about a cup of the stuffing leftover so I crushed some sliced almonds and made a cheese ball. That vanished too!

I made these but I'm used to making with breading type stuffing and herbs and a little prosciutto and those are fantastic. I made this with 4 times the ingredients and 48 mushrooms. I had at least 10 oz of cream cheese mix left over. Too much. And that was with generous filling. I used Fat Free cream cheese. All in all, the recipe is mostly cream cheese! That's all you taste and it sits like lead in your gut 2 hours later. Never again. I would ditch the cream cheese and go with a bread crumb filling. Far less fat. Only people who "love" cream cheese will like this. Or, maybe cut the cream cheese in half and add bread crumbs to the other half. Might work.

Hubby loved them! I added cut up shrimps and mixed it all together with the Philly and spices. I topped it with some havarti (or your favourite cheese) and 2 finely sliced red pepper on top for some colour.

Yumm! I omitted the cayenne because my stomach is having issues and sprinkled with shredded parmesan before cooking. Was very good and will make again. I think some crisp bacon on top would be an excellent finishing touch.

I used a standard 8-ounce package of mushrooms; I felt that if I removed the stems and added a full 8 ounces of cream, the leftovers would end up in a real mess, so I decided to try using half the amount instead.,
Made as directed except I substituted 2 tablespoons jalapeno jelly instead of the cayenne pepper. It was amazing!

I gave it a 2 star just because it was an easy recipe. My husband and I did not like the taste. Way too much cream cheese and I hated the heat of the Cheyanne pepper. Less cream cheese, more breadcrumbs l, and instead of Cheyanne pepper, I may try smoked paprika. I followed the recipe to a T and will not make it that way again.
I added bacon, green onions, and cheddar cheese to the mixture. Sprinkled shredded cheddar on top. Always a hit!!

Perfect for Lent! I did not put the Parmesan cheese in the filling, but sprinkled it on top before baking. Also, I added the breadcrumbs and a diced red pimiento (broiled pepper) for a decorative kick.
Very good recipe, added 2 tubes of grated/finely chopped imitation crab to the pan of shallots and mushroom stems. Topped with panko as suggested.
Delicious and easy recipe. Will definitely make again!
